title: Golem IR names, types and declarations
description: §18.2 IR building blocks: qualified names, type references, source spans and the declarations of the types, failures and notices sections. The full grammars are in CONTRACTS.md ('Names' and 'Type references'); JSON Schema patterns here are coarse and scripts/check-ir.mjs parses every name and type exactly.

QualifiedName.description: §6.4, §6.7, §18.2 PD-14 fully qualified name of a task, fn, const, type, failure, notice or activity after monomorphization: module path, optional receiver type for members, simple name, type arguments for instances of generic declarations (open<golem.windows.Container>), and a parameter-type signature when the name's overload set has more than one member (golem.core.goto(Goal,Int,PathOpts)). Prelude and built-in names have no module (Bot.food, min(Int,Int), Goal). Grammar in CONTRACTS.md 'Names'.

TypeRef.description: §6.1-§6.4, §18.2 PD-15 type reference as a canonical string: a built-in or qualified declared type name, type arguments in <...> separated by ',' without spaces, and a trailing '?' for optionals, as in List<BlockPos>, Window<golem.windows.Container>?, Map<ItemType,Int>. Aliases are resolved (SlotRange is written Range). Grammar in CONTRACTS.md 'Type references'.

LocalName.description: §10.1 PD-17 frame-local slot name: a source IDENT, renamed name~n when it shadows an earlier local of the same frame, or a compiler temporary $kind<n> ($t0 temporary, $i0 iterator, $c0 counter, $o0 optional binder, $v0 variant).

Resource.description: §2, §13.3 physical resources, in canonical order legs, head, hands, stance, inventory, screen; resource sets are written in this order without duplicates.

ResourceSet.description: §13.3 a set of resources in canonical order (check-ir enforces the order).

Span.description: §18.2 PD-16 compact source span of an IR node: [file, line, column, end_line, end_column], with file an index into header.sources, lines and columns 1-based, columns in Unicode code points, end exclusive.

SourceFile.description: §18.2 header: one source file the bot reaches, with its content hash. Std modules use std/golem/<module>.golem (PD-36).

Param.description: §9.9 parameter of a task, fn, job or activity: name, resolved type and, when declared, the default as a constant wire value (§6.3: defaults are constant expressions). A receiver is the parameter named self.

FieldDecl.description: §6.3 struct, variant, failure or notice field: name, resolved type and optional constant default in wire form.

TypeDecl.description: §18.2 types section entry: a struct (window kinds are empty structs with window_kind data) or an enum, monomorphized, with derived trait flags (§6.3).

DerivedTraits.description: §6.3, §6.6 which of Eq, Ord, Wire the type implements; each is derived independently.

StructDecl.description: §6.3 struct with fields in declaration order.

WindowKindInfo.description: §17.4 window kind data of an empty kind struct: its menu types (WindowKind.menu_types()), the capability traits it implements and, for CraftingStation kinds, its grid size.

EnumDecl.description: §6.3 enum with variants in declaration order (the order Ord uses).

FailureDecl.description: §18.2 failures section entry: a user-declared failure with its wire name (the simple name used as type in reports, §16.2) and wire field types. Built-in failures (§16.1) are fixed by the spec and not listed.

NoticeDecl.description: §18.2 notices section entry: a notice with its wire name (notice report name, §16.2) and wire field types.
